parsed.why: State enforces against gender presentation: trans women jailed five years for wearing women's clothing, appearance-based convictions, police extortion, beatings in custody, no recourse and shuttered LGBT groups. Imprisonment with state's own hand.

No criminalisation and no state hostility, but zero protections and documented impunity: police dismiss trans complainants because ID reads male, healthcare refusal, elevated assault risk. Thin recourse keeps it below the reduced band.

Strong operating protections — GI covered in goods and services, hate-speech law, arrests after the 2024 mob attack — offset by social chill (35% openness vs 51% regional) and default custody/police practice by registered sex.

State-directed targeting: police sweep and document trans women in the street, 299 detention decisions in 2025, hostile official rhetoric and draft criminalisation, custody death uninvestigated, ID-carry rule pulls visitors into stops.

No criminalisation of gender expression, court rulings and self-declared markers give real institutional recourse, but documented public harassment of visibly trans people in provincial cities plus rising official hate speech and threats.
